newsitem.title: LATVIA: BALTICS-VILNIUS, RIGA DIVIDED ON CUSTOMS UNION.
newsitem.headline: BALTICS-VILNIUS, RIGA DIVIDED ON CUSTOMS UNION.

text.p: Lithuania and Latvia aired their differences on Monday about the creation of a Baltic customs Union.

Latvia sees such a move as an essential step on the road to the EU but Lithuania said it was not a pressing issue and that its absence would pose no obstacle to Baltic integration into the coveted European club.

"We do not think that we have to first create a customs union and only then go to the EU," Lithuania's foreign minister Algirdas Saudargas told a news conference. Saudargas was in Latvia for a one-day official visit.
"Next year, we hope, we will start accession talks with the EU and that will absorb all our energy and we are measuring all our other co-operation with this main process in mind," Saudargas said.
"Our attitude towards the customs union has to be viewed in the context of our integration into the EU," he said.

"The creation of a customs union would enhance the integration of the Baltic states into the EU," Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele stressed during his meeting with Saudargas, the government press office said in a statement.
"It would make the way of Baltic-made goods into the Europan market easier," the statement also said.
